hook: Content note: the file deals frankly with constant pain, sex as a transmission route, and hosts who kill themselves. The premise is a living tattoo, an ornate dragon that moves across a person's skin, and the article is short and matter-of-fact. Its strength lies in how calmly it lists details that ought to be alarming.
whyItMatters: It is a Safe entry that shows how much can be done with one striking image and a clinical voice. The Safe label sits uneasily next to what hosting the dragon actually costs, since easy containment for the Foundation means endless pain for whoever carries it. It also raises a question the file admits it cannot answer: how do you study a creature that exists in only two dimensions?
thingsToNotice:
The procedures quietly reveal that Class-D personnel are normally subject to monthly termination, and that carrying the dragon is the only thing exempting its host. The very first caption, naming a previous host who is now dead, tells you how that deal tends to end.

The feeding details are oddly charming, with ink simply vanishing and staff 'feeding' it by quickly tattooing fruit or small animals onto the host, yet every movement it makes feels like being tattooed and having tattoos removed at the same time. Transfer is handled with the same flat tone: sex works 93% of the time but is too painful to be practical, so pressing two open wounds together is preferred, and it can even be moved off a corpse. The perks of extra strength, confidence and immunity are listed right before the admission that a number of hosts have committed suicide and a few died of skin infections.

The last paragraph pulls back to the dragon's possible age of centuries, implying a long, untraceable chain of people who carried it before the Foundation did.
